commentary_segments.text: Resistors are little more than a conductive island contacted at both extremities. Many different resistors can be realized as many different diffused or ion implanted islands can be realized. Some examples are given in this slide. Normally the smaller dimension, which is W in the example at the bottom, determines the matching which can be achieved. In bipolar technologies, several diffusion layers can be identified, such as the ones for the base, for the emitter, for the collector, etc. In CMOS technologies however, the source and drain diffusion is always available. Also the well-diffusion can be used for high-valued resistances. They are all listed next.
